source: Crossfield et al. (2020), ApJL 903, L7, 'Phase Curves of Hot Neptune LTT 9779b Suggest a High-metallicity Atmosphere' (doi:10.3847/2041-8213/abbc71; arXiv:2010.12745). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um phase curve, program GO-14290. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source: the table of fit and derived parameters and the table that compares the data with models, row 'Spitzer 4.5 um, data'. The model is one sinusoid (their phase-curve equation); the comparison table's notes define its amplitude as peak-to-valley and its offset as the eastward shift of the maximum from the substellar point. The day-side flux is the eclipse depth of Dragomir et al. (2020), which the fit holds fixed.

radiusRatio.where: table of fit parameters, R_p/R_*, 4.5 um, this work

eclipseDepth.cell: 375 +/- 62 ppm, F_P/F_* at phase 0.5, from Dragomir et al. (2020)
eclipseDepth.where: comparison table, Spitzer 4.5 um, data, F_P/F_* at phi = 0.5

model.equation: f(phi) = 1 - A cos(phi - Delta phi), phi the orbital phase from transit; the tables print the peak-to-valley amplitude and the eastward shift of the maximum.

semiAmplitude.cell: 358 +/- 106 ppm peak-to-valley (table note a): half of it is the semi-amplitude, 179 ppm
semiAmplitude.where: comparison table, Spitzer 4.5 um, data, Amplitude

offsetDegreesEast.cell: -10 +/- 21 degrees east of the substellar point: slightly west (table note)
offsetDegreesEast.where: comparison table, Spitzer 4.5 um, data, Offset

daysideK.where: table of derived parameters, T_day, 4.5 um

nightsideK.where: table of derived parameters, T_night, 4.5 um

offsetDegrees.where: comparison table, Spitzer 4.5 um, data, Offset
